subjects.subject: app-shell
subjects.evidence: Architecture check first: this is a Next.js SPA-shell (app/page.tsx mounts Workspace.tsx once; tab switches are client state, not route navigation), so the golden path's literal 'shell never unmounts' property holds and the hosting/nav-hierarchy rules apply without the frame-continuity correction's alternate reading. nav-hierarchy is mostly realized (NavSectionRail.tsx:163-219 two-level rail+panel, section-scoped; aria-pressed on preview vs aria-current="page" only on the real destination — NavSectionRail.tsx:147, NavPanelItem.tsx:79,85) but NavRailPreferences.tsx:98 exposes the appearance/language triggers' name reveal via the native `title` attribute only, which fails SC 1.4.13 (not Dismissible/Hoverable/Persistent) — the technique's own 'name for AT vs reveal for the eye are two obligations' correction, unmet on the second obligation. badge-and-attention also falls short: WorkspaceNav.tsx/NavPanelItem.tsx render exactly one severity grade (a coral count pill) folding 'failed, needs a decision' and 'N things waiting' into the same integer, and NavSectionRail.tsx's level-one rail button shows no parent-aggregated roll-up of its group's badges, so an unpreviewed section's attention is invisible.

subjects.subject: voice-io
subjects.evidence: This context is the strongest realization of duplex-agent-sessions in the tree. index.ts:49-70 and candidate-brief.ts implement the audience-safe-brief allow-list explicitly (candidate-brief.ts:11-19: 'THE SECURITY BOUNDARY IS THE SANITIZER IN THIS FILE... never turn this into a deny-list'), with candidateSafeTopic() scrubbing bracketed assessment asides out of topic labels (candidate-brief.ts:76-87). eleven-agent-diff.mjs is the drift gate the technique asks for: a pure, network-free field-by-field diff between intended and live agent config, defensive-read so a shape change degrades to reported drift rather than a crash (never silently reads as agreement). finalize-status.ts computes a real end-of-call verdict rather than trusting the close event (interviewFinalStatus distinguishes a late-blip-on-a-substantive-call from a real abandonment, and unmountBeaconStatus separately handles the late-arrival/in-flight-End case). connect-failover.ts deliberately builds the served provider's prompt OUTSIDE the failover trigger so a failing brief-build surfaces as itself rather than masquerading as a second real failover (connect-failover.ts:72-78).
